body.statement: If \(f\), \(\theta'\), and \(\kappa\) are constant on \(J\), then \(T_n(P)=n^{1/3}|J|\{f\theta'^2/(4\kappa)\}^{1/3}\); once this deterministic horizon lies in \([T_0,\infty)\), Theorems 1--3 reduce to a stationary canonical LR maximum on that interval. At one fixed dose, the marginal statistic reduces to the Banerjee--Wellner law \(D(0)\).
body.justification: The reduction checks both the spatial factor and the fixed-point normalization against known theory.
body.gap: The fixed-dose reduction is known from Banerjee and Wellner (2001); the growing deterministic interval is the new simultaneous component.
body.consumer: The constant-coefficient clock and fixed-dose reduction are valid diagnostics, not a proof of the growing-domain law.

obligation.what_is_open: The homogeneous clock and fixed-location identities are proved, but the proposition's invocation of the three growing-domain inference theorems cannot be certified while those theorems remain open.
obligation.obstruction: Constant-coefficient substitution determines the interval length and fixed-origin functional but supplies no canonical excursion, causal transfer, or feasible calibration law.
obligation.attempted: The spatial integral was evaluated exactly, the canonical coordinate was shown affine, and translation of one constraint location to the origin was checked.
obligation.partial_result:
If \(f(a)=f_0\), \(\theta'(a)=r_0\), and \(\kappa(a)=\kappa_0\) on \(J\), substitution into \(\texttt{def:spatial-clock}\) gives
\[
\mathcal V(P)=|J|\left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3},
\qquad
T_n(P)=n^{1/3}|J|\left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3}.
\]
The canonical coordinate is affine in dose and maps \(J\) to an interval of exactly this length.  At one fixed dose, translation puts the constraint at the origin, and the local functional is \(D(0)\) by \(\texttt{def:canonical-field}\).  These algebraic identities do not prove the unresolved growing-domain excursion, transfer, or calibration assertions.
